glossary.RIR: RIR is the number of reps you could still complete before failure. RIR 2 means two reps left. If you are new to RIR, estimate whether you could do one or two more.
glossary.rep range: A rep range is the minimum and maximum reps for each set, such as 4 to 8. Add weight after every set reaches the maximum.
glossary.double progression: Add reps until every set reaches the top of the range. Then add weight and return to the bottom.
glossary.deload: A deload is a lighter session that gives you more time to recover after progress stalls.
glossary.e1RM: Taurifer estimates your one-rep max with the Epley formula: load × (1 + reps/30). Use it to compare hard sets across sessions.
glossary.hard set: A hard set ends at or below your hard-set RIR ceiling. Taurifer counts these sets in the volume audit.
glossary.Easy effort: Choose Easy when you could complete about three more reps, or RIR 3.
glossary.Hard effort: Choose Hard when you could complete about one more rep, or RIR 1.
glossary.Max effort: Choose Max at or near failure, or RIR 0. Use it for your last set or when the program calls for it.
glossary.Effort: Easy maps to RIR 3, Hard to RIR 1, and Max to RIR 0. Taurifer uses that value in its load recommendations.

tour.0.body: Workout logs, drafts, and history stay on this device. Taurifer never uploads them. Setup links share a program, its configuration, eight selected settings, and the app language. They never include workout history. Choose Next to see each part of the app, or Skip tour to close this guide.
tour.1.body: Choose a training day and date. Enter the load, reps, and RIR for each set. Taurifer uses your history to recommend when to add load.
tour.2.body: Use List to see the full session. Use Focus to log one exercise at a time on a phone.
tour.3.body: In Focus, swipe the card or use the header arrows to change exercises. Enter a load, reps, and RIR, then tap Log set. Tap a logged set to edit it. To log by voice, enable the microphone in Settings and open the ⋯ menu.
tour.4.body: The header rest control in Focus starts and stops the timer. On Today, the orange dot counts exercises ready for more weight.
tour.rest_preview_hint: Rest is off. Enable it in Settings to use the timer.
tour.5.body: Tap Finish workout to save the session. Stats and History then include it. Taurifer shows rest and backup reminders when they are due.
tour.6.body: Use Overview for weekly totals, Strength for load trends, Volume for hard sets, PRs for records, and Review for block analysis. Open Charts and tables for per-exercise data.
tour.7.body: History contains every saved session and set. Open a session to review or correct it.
tour.8.body: Add days and exercises in the program editor. Set muscles and rep ranges for each exercise. Use End block to review the current block and choose what comes next.
tour.9.body: Set your units, RIR entry, and progression rules here. Export regular backups because Taurifer stores your data only on this device.

rec.repgoal.advance.label: Add load
rec.repgoal.advance.text: You hit the {goal}-rep total at a manageable effort. Add weight and rebuild the total.
rec.repgoal.rebuild.label: Add load
rec.repgoal.rebuild.text: You hit the {goal}-rep total, so the load goes up. Start at {reps} reps a set and climb back to {goal}.
rec.repgoal.effort.label: Hold · recover
rec.repgoal.effort.text: You reached {goal} reps, but the sets were too hard to add weight yet. Hold the load.
rec.repgoal.progress.label: Chase the total
rec.repgoal.progress.text: You finished {done} of {goal} reps. Hold the load and close the gap.
rec.repgoal.reduce.label: Back off
rec.repgoal.reduce.text: You can no longer reach {floor} reps a set at this load. Reduce it.
rec.repgoal.session.label: Total so far
rec.repgoal.session.text: {done} of {goal} reps done. Aim for {reps} on this set.
rec.repgoal.session.done.label: Total complete
rec.repgoal.session.done.text: All {sets} sets are logged. You finished {done} of {goal} reps.
rec.anchor.new.label: New lift
rec.anchor.new.text: No history yet. Pick a top-set load you can hold for {min}-{max} reps, then take {backoffs} lighter sets.
rec.anchor.advance.label: Add load
rec.anchor.advance.text: Your top set reached {max} reps with effort to spare. Add weight; the lighter sets follow it up.
rec.anchor.hold.label: Hold
rec.anchor.hold.text: Your top set is still inside {min}-{max} reps. Hold the load and add reps.
rec.anchor.reduce.label: Back off
rec.anchor.reduce.text: Your top set fell below {min} reps. Bring it down one step; the lighter sets follow it down.
rec.anchor.session.label: Lighter sets
rec.anchor.session.text: Based on the top set you just did, take the rest at {load} {unit} for {reps} reps.
rec.anchor.recalibrate.label: Recalibrate
rec.anchor.recalibrate.text: The top set came in under {min} reps. The remaining sets are rebuilt from what you actually lifted.
rec.anchor.session.done.label: Sets complete
rec.anchor.session.done.text: Every set for this lift is logged.
rec.anchor.insufficient.label: Log the top set
rec.anchor.insufficient.text: The lighter sets come from your top set. Log it first and they will fill in.
why.repgoal.total: You finished {done} of the {goal}-rep total across {sets} sets.
why.repgoal.effort: Your typical effort was about {rir} RIR, and adding weight needs at least {min}.
why.repgoal.distribution: The remaining reps are spread across the sets you have not logged yet.
why.repgoal.rebuild: The total stays {goal}. At the new load you start at {reps} a set and build back to it.
why.anchor.top: Your top set was {load} {unit} for {reps} reps.
why.anchor.backoff: The lighter sets are {percent}% of the top set, which comes to {load} {unit}.
why.anchor.untouched: Only the sets you have not logged yet were updated.
rec.effort.new.label: New lift
rec.effort.new.text: No history yet. Choose a load for {reps} reps with {min}-{max} reps in reserve.
rec.effort.advance.label: Add load
rec.effort.advance.text: You completed {reps} reps with more than {max} reps in reserve. Add one load step.
rec.effort.hold.label: Hold
rec.effort.hold.text: Keep this load for {reps} reps at {min}-{max} reps in reserve.
rec.effort.reduce.label: Back off
rec.effort.rep_miss.text: You missed the {reps}-rep target. Reduce one load step.
rec.effort.too_hard.text: You finished below {min} reps in reserve. Reduce one load step.
rec.effort.no_rir.label: Hold · log effort
rec.effort.no_rir.text: The load is usable, but there is no effort entry to justify changing it. Hold.
why.effort.evidence: The latest comparable work was {load} {unit} for {reps} reps at {rir} RIR.
why.effort.target: The authored target stays {reps} reps at {min}-{max} RIR.
why.effort.grid: The actionable load grid puts the target at {load} {unit}.

entry.save_failed.body: Your active program was not changed. Keep this page open and try again.

entry.rules_changed.title: Program rules have changed
entry.rules_changed.body: A saved preview is still here. Rebuild with current rules before activating a current-version program, or keep the pinned preview if it remains executable.
entry.conflict.title: Your active program changed
entry.conflict.body: Another change updated the active program while this setup was open. Review again before replacing it.

entry.result.explain: Based on your desired result, recent training state, schedule, and main constraint.
entry.result.why_schedule: It fits {days} days with sessions capped at {minutes} minutes.
entry.result.why_reductions: The first week reduces work in {n} bounded places to match your recent training.
entry.result.why_compromises: It makes {n} bounded compromises to fit your constraints.
entry.result.why_interrupted: Because you completed about half of your recent training, the first week temporarily reduces work before the normal program resumes.
